title: Booster pump startup: remote check-through
equipment: Hyfab booster pump skid (up to 5 pumps, PLC and VFD)

n1.text: Ask the tech to confirm pre-power MECHANICAL checks: motor bolts, discharge flanges, pump base, flange and Victaulic connections all tight?

r_mech.cause: Mechanical connections are not secure, so the skid is not ready for power.
fix: Have the tech tighten the loose bolts, flanges or Victaulic connections, then restart this check.

n2.text: Pre-power ELECTRICAL: motor wiring correct and tight; control breaker (line and load) and terminal strip wires tight; components secure; inverter inspected with cover removed (wiring tight, components secure); control transformer has proper primary and secondary voltage and tight wires. All good?

fix: Have a qualified tech correct the wiring, loose terminations or transformer voltage problem before applying power.
Do not energize the skid until every item on the pre-power list is good.

n3.text: Initial power-up: horizontal pumps primed with air bled from the top and couplings correct and tight? Vertical pumps with shaft/impellers adjusted to the blue spacer tool?

r_prime.cause: Pumps are not prepared to run.
fix: Have the tech prime horizontal pumps, bleed air from the top, and check the couplings.
Adjust vertical pump shaft and impellers to the blue spacer tool, then continue.

n4.text: Has rotation been checked on every pump (pump 1 through 5 as applicable)?

r_rot.cause: Pump rotation is unverified or wrong.
fix: Have the tech check rotation on each pump before running further and correct any that are reversed per the pump manual.

n5.text: Ask the tech to measure supply voltage A-B, B-C, A-C and each phase to ground, plus control voltage. Is any reading over 506 VAC on a 460 VAC system (+10% of station design), or control voltage over 132 VAC?

r_volt.cause: Supply or control voltage is above the limit on the Hyfab startup sheet.
fix: Do not run the skid. Have a qualified electrician find and correct the over-voltage with the utility or source.
Limits on the sheet: not to exceed 506 VAC on 460 VAC systems (+10% of station design); control voltage not to exceed 132 VAC.

r_done.cause: Checks complete; the rest is recording data.
fix: Have the tech record motor nameplate data, PLC and VFD manufacturer, model, serial and software version, and the operating macro.
Record the safety settings: low discharge pressure, high inlet pressure, high discharge pressure, high pump temperature setpoint and low inlet pressure.
